title: My Teammate
mood: Rivals made one team, a box of chocolate, and a raid by the sea beside the Academy’s famous pair.

hero.alt: Fanny smiles warmly as she speaks, in her white shirt and red bow tie.
hero.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: On the tenth morning, Layla and Fanny were both in the drill hall by half past four when Professor Joe walked in on a cane. His shoulder was strapped, and his two ribs made him stand stiffly.
“Team B3 is dissolved,” he said. “Roger has gone to another pair. He reports that he falls down less. You two are the Layla-Fanny Team. Mine. Exclusive.”
Layla had refused eleven partnership offers in two years. “I didn’t agree to that.”
“It isn’t a vote. Aspirants fight in pairs. The suits decided that, not the Academy. Two who trust each other pull more out of a suit than the same two apart, and nobody has ever explained why.”
He pointed his cane at the window. Across the courtyard, the billboard of Guinevere and Vexana was lit. “Those two are undefeated. Ask them why. They can’t tell you either.”
“From today you share one score. A kill is a point. A civilian carried clear is ten.”
One score meant nobody on the team to beat. Fanny said, “Understood.”
Joe ticked both names on the pairing sheet with his stylus, two small marks with the same slant. “I pair on hours, not scores. You two put in the most hours in my year.”
Layla took that to mean the drill hall’s sign-in sheets. She kept her own score anyway.
In freeform training, the drones came at them in a flock. Layla’s cannon took one clean out of the air. It hit the floor at her feet, its eyes two little crosses.

media.alt: In freeform training Layla fires her cannon, and one drone drops at her feet with crosses for eyes.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: Fanny took the rest. Her cables shot out, and she swung through the flock with her blades. Drones rained down around her.
When it was over, Fanny stood in a heap of wrecks. Layla stood beside her one drone and glared at it.
“Why am I always the one getting hurt...?”

blocks.caption: Why am I always the one getting hurt...?

segs.t: Fanny looked at her, puzzled. Nobody had touched her.

media.alt: Fanny slashes through a flock of drones, then stands puzzled beside a scowling Layla and a heap of wrecks.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: Jump training was on the Academy roofs. Layla backed up to the rail, ran and leaped the gap. She landed among the dishes on the far roof. A score flashed up beside her: 10 POINTS. She spread her arms wide.

media.alt: Layla smirks, leaps the gap between roofs and lands with her arms spread, scoring 10 points.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: Wind hit her from behind. Fanny went past on her cables, over that gap and the next, and landed on a roof two floors higher.
Layla stood there with her arms still out.

media.alt: Fanny streaks past on her cables and lands on a much higher roof while Layla gapes from below.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: Then came the day the whole Academy traded chocolate. Layla walked down the corridor with nineteen boxes stacked to her chin. “Hah, you won’t be beating me this time!”

blocks.caption: Hah, you won’t be beating me this time!

media.alt: Layla beams over a tall stack of wrapped gift boxes, then smiles a smug little smile.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: Fanny came in at the far door. Her hands were empty.

media.alt: Layla holds a gift box and watches Fanny walk in through a door with nothing in her hands.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: Ah, she didn’t get chocolate, did she?

blocks.caption: Ah, she didn’t get chocolate, did she?

segs.t: Layla hid her smile behind her hand. “Fanny, did you get any chocolate? I’ve received tons!”

blocks.caption: Fanny, did you get any chocolate? I’ve received tons!

segs.t: Fanny glanced over her shoulder. Behind her, boxes stood stacked in a wall. Layla counted twenty-six.
“Humph.” She turned her back on the wall.

media.alt: A wall of gift boxes appears beside Fanny, and Layla stares, then turns her back in a huff.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: In class she sat with her arms folded and glared at her desk. “I’ll win next time for sure!”

blocks.caption: I’ll win next time for sure!

segs.t: A pink box with a teal ribbon came down on the desk in front of her. Fanny had both hands on it.

media.alt: Layla sulks at her desk, arms folded, until Fanny sets a pink box with a teal ribbon in front of her.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: “This is for you, my teammate!”

blocks.caption: This is for you, my teammate!

segs.t: “For me? Well..... It’d sure be rude of me not to accept your kind gift!”

blocks.caption: For me? Well..... It’d sure be rude of me not to accept your kind gift!

media.alt: Layla jumps in surprise at her desk, then pouts and keeps the box while Fanny stands beside her.
media.credit: Official short animation, Layla and Fanny

segs.t: That night, in the lab, Layla set the box on the top shelf beside the trophy, ribbon facing the room.

The Enders no longer came in waves, only handfuls. The third years went through the gate portal day after day. Layla took charge, because somebody had to, and went first, so that Fanny would be covered. Fanny followed with a frown.
She wants to go first,
thought Layla. She let her have the frown.
The raid that mattered was on a shore ward. At the portal, a pink-haired girl stopped in front of Layla with her chin up.

media.alt: Terrinia from high above: towers around a blue bay that opens to the sea, a great tower sending light into the sky.

segs.t: “You’re Layla. I’m the great lady Guinevere. Nobody’s introduced us.”
“You’re on a billboard.”
“Yes,” said Guinevere, delighted. “That’s me.”
“Vexana,” said the black-haired girl beside her, in case it was needed. Her eyes were violet, and a small mole sat beside her mouth.

blocks.caption: Guinevere and Vexana, the Academy’s undefeated pair.

media.alt: A small drawing of the pair: black-haired Vexana smiling faintly behind pink-haired Guinevere, who cheers with a fist up.

segs.t: “Layla-Fanny Team, the market’s west end,” said the command channel. “Guinevere and Vexana, the east end.”
The fish market, the west end.
Enders dropped onto the market stalls through a tear in the dome. Under the awnings, people still crouched among the crates.
“Ten points a civilian,” said Layla. “I keep them off. You carry.”
“Let’s do our best together.”
Fanny’s cables shot out. She dropped under the awnings and rose again with a woman on one arm and a boy on the other. From a stall roof, Layla shot whatever turned toward them.
Each trip took Fanny nine seconds. Layla started counting trips instead of kills.
The east end, the same minute.
Guinevere hung in the mouth of the tear on wings of light. Two gray drones circled her shoulders, their eyes yellow rings. Drones and wings both ran on her aspirant power.
She met the Enders with her fists. Whatever she knocked back, Vexana’s staff finished from the roof below. Guinevere never looked back to check.
Vexana is there.

media.alt: Guinevere and Vexana fight back to back among Enders, Guinevere with her fists up and two cat-eared drones, Vexana with her staff.

segs.t: “Light of day, pour down.”
Light poured from her drones and threw three Enders back through the tear.
Around the thirtieth minute, the drones flew a hand lower. Their rings dimmed a shade each pass.
A great lady does not land early,
thought Guinevere. She kept her back straight.
The east end, a roof.
Vexana had watched the drones sag for a minute. She did not call out. Told to rest, Guinevere only flew higher.
Then the wings went out like a switch.
Guinevere dropped past the roofline. Vexana leaned from the edge, caught her wrist, and hauled her up without a word. The drones hung dark. Guinevere raised her chin.
“Ngh... this is a lady’s refinement. It’s the way to regain your elegance in three seconds.”
Vexana counted. It took four. Then one ring lit, and the other.
“Four,” said Vexana.
Her own hand was shaking. She closed it on her staff until it stopped.
I saw it a minute ago. I said nothing.
She kept a step closer to Guinevere for the rest of the raid.
The west end.
Fanny set the last family down behind the fish hall. Fourteen carried clear. Across the market, the pink-haired girl was back in the air, the black-haired one on the roof below her.
The tear still hung open. Fanny landed two roofs over, frowning at Layla again. Layla went first.
